docs.title: spacy-conll
docs.text:
spacy-conll converts the output of a spaCy pipeline to CoNLL-U and reads CoNLL-U back into spaCy Doc objects. It is a spaCy pipeline component (conll_formatter), a ConllParser class for text and files, and a command line tool (parse-as-conll).

The library formats what a parser predicts. The tags in the output come from the model that you use. The English spaCy models do not use Universal Dependencies labels. If you need UD labels, use the UDPipe backend (spacy-udpipe), which loads models that are trained on UD data.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install spacy-conll

This installs spaCy as the only dependency. Extras add optional features:

pip install "spacy-conll[udpipe]"  # UDPipe backend through spacy-udpipe
pip install "spacy-conll[pd]"      # pandas DataFrames in `._.conll_pd`
pip install "spacy-conll[all]"     # udpipe and pandas

spacy-conll[parsers] is an alias of spacy-conll[udpipe]. spacy-conll needs Python 3.11 or newer and spaCy 3.8 or newer.

spaCy models are not part of the install. Download the model that you want to use, for example:

python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Add conll_formatter as the last component of a pipeline and read the CoNLL-U output from the Doc:

import spacy

nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
nlp.add_pipe("conll_formatter", last=True)

doc = nlp("I like cookies. What about you?")
print(doc._.conll_str)

1   I   I   PRON    PRP Case=Nom|Number=Sing|Person=1|PronType=Prs  2   nsubj   _   _
2   like    like    VERB    VBP Tense=Pres|VerbForm=Fin 0   root    _   _
3   cookies cooky   NOUN    NNS Number=Plur 2   dobj    _   SpaceAfter=No
4   .   .   PUNCT   .   PunctType=Peri  2   punct   _   _

1   What    what    PRON    WP  _   2   dep _   _
2   about   about   ADP IN  _   0   root    _   _
3   you you PRON    PRP Case=Acc|Person=2|PronType=Prs  2   pobj    _   SpaceAfter=No
4   ?   ?   PUNCT   .   PunctType=Peri  2   punct   _   SpaceAfter=No

init_parser builds a pipeline with the formatter in one call, and the command line tool parses text without any Python code:

parse-as-conll en_core_web_sm spacy --input-str "I like cookies." --include-headers

The usage guide describes all options. Coming from v4? Read the migration guide.

docs.title: spacy_conll.formatter
docs.text: The conll_formatter pipeline component.

docs.title: ConllFormatter dataclass
docs.text:
ConllFormatter(
    conversion_maps: dict[str, dict[str, str]]
    | None = None,
    ext_names: dict[str, str] = dict(),
    field_names: dict[str, str] = dict(),
    include_headers: bool = False,
    disable_pandas: bool = False,
    columns: list[str] | None = None,
)

spaCy component that adds CoNLL-U representations to docs, sentences and tokens.

The extension conll holds a dict of field names to values on a Token, a list of those dicts on a sentence Span, and a list of sentence lists on a Doc. The extension conll_str holds the tab-separated CoNLL-U text, and conll_pd (when pandas is installed and disable_pandas is false) holds a pandas Series or DataFrame. The pandas object is built from conll on access and is not stored in the doc, so docs can be saved with DocBin and sent between processes. Multi-word tokens and empty nodes are not supported.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default conversion_maps dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None

Maps a field name to a map of output values, for example {"LEMMA": {"-PRON-": "PRON"}} replaces the lemma -PRON- with PRON.

None ext_names dict[str, str]

New names for the extensions conll, conll_str and conll_pd, for example {"conll": "conll_dict"}.

dict() field_names dict[str, str]

New names for the CoNLL-U fields ID, FORM, LEMMA, UPOS, XPOS, FEATS, HEAD, DEPREL, DEPS and MISC, for example {"UPOS": "upostag"}.

dict() include_headers bool

Whether conll_str of a sentence starts with the # sent_id and # text comment lines.

False disable_pandas bool

Whether to skip the conll_pd extension even if pandas is installed.

False columns list[str] | None

The CoNLL-U Plus columns to write, in this order. None uses Doc._.conll_columns if the doc has it (a doc that was read from CoNLL-U Plus text), and plain CoNLL-U otherwise. With columns, conll_str of the doc starts with a # global.columns line. The names are the CoNLL-U names (also when field_names renames them) or custom names such as PARSEME:MWE. A custom column takes its value from the dict in Token._.conll_custom_columns, and is _ when the dict does not have it.

None

Examples:

import spacy
nlp = spacy.blank("en")
_ = nlp.add_pipe("sentencizer")
_ = nlp.add_pipe(
    "conll_formatter", config={"include_headers": True}
)
doc = nlp("Hello world.")
doc[1]._.conll
# {'ID': 2, 'FORM': 'world', 'LEMMA': '_', 'UPOS': '_', 'XPOS': '_',
#  'FEATS': '_', 'HEAD': '_', 'DEPREL': '_', 'DEPS': '_',
#  'MISC': 'SpaceAfter=No'}
print(doc._.conll_str.replace("\t", " "))
# # sent_id = 1
# # text = Hello world.
# 1 Hello _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
# 2 world _ _ _ _ _ _ _ SpaceAfter=No
# 3 . _ _ _ _ _ _ _ SpaceAfter=No

docs.title: get_whitespace_misc
docs.text:
get_whitespace_misc(token: Token) -> str

Describe the whitespace around a token in the MISC notation of UD.

The whitespace after a token is its own trailing space plus the text of the whitespace tokens that follow it, also when these tokens belong to the next sentence. A single space gives _, no whitespace gives SpaceAfter=No and anything else gives SpacesAfter with the escapes \s, \t, \n and \r. Whitespace at the start of the doc gives SpacesBefore on the first token that is not whitespace. See https://universaldependencies.org/misc.html.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default token Token

A token that is not whitespace.

required

Returns:

Type Description str

The MISC value.

Examples:

import spacy
doc = spacy.blank("en")("\nHello  world.\t")
[t.text for t in doc]
# ['\n', 'Hello', ' ', 'world', '.', '\t']
[get_whitespace_misc(t) for t in doc if not t.is_space]
# ['SpacesAfter=\\s\\s|SpacesBefore=\\n', 'SpaceAfter=No', 'SpacesAfter=\\t']

View source on GitHub: src/spacy_conll/formatter.py lines 77–123

docs.title: merge_misc
docs.text:
merge_misc(misc: str, whitespace_misc: str) -> str

Replace the whitespace entries in a MISC value and keep the others.

The entries SpaceAfter, SpacesAfter and SpacesBefore of misc are replaced by those of whitespace_misc in the same position, or removed when whitespace_misc has no such entry. New whitespace entries go at the end. spaCy stores the whitespace after a token as a single space or nothing, so an existing SpacesAfter (for example read from a CoNLL-U file) stays when the token is followed by a single space. An existing SpacesBefore stays when whitespace_misc has none.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default misc str

The current MISC value, _ if empty.

required whitespace_misc str

The output of get_whitespace_misc.

required

Returns:

Type Description str

The merged MISC value, _ if empty.

Examples:

merge_misc("Translit=a|SpaceAfter=No", "_")
# 'Translit=a'
merge_misc("Translit=a", "SpaceAfter=No")
# 'Translit=a|SpaceAfter=No'
merge_misc("SpacesAfter=\\n|Translit=a", "_")
# 'SpacesAfter=\\n|Translit=a'
merge_misc("SpacesAfter=\\n|Translit=a", "SpaceAfter=No")
# 'Translit=a|SpaceAfter=No'
merge_misc("SpacesBefore=\\n|Translit=a", "_")
# 'SpacesBefore=\\n|Translit=a'

docs.title: parse_text_as_conll
docs.text:
parse_text_as_conll(
    text: str,
    *,
    n_process: int = 1,
    renumber_sent_ids: bool = True,
    ignore_pipe_errors: bool = False,
    split_on_newline: bool = True,
    sent_ids: Iterable[str | int] | None = None,
) -> str

Parse a text and return its CoNLL-U representation.

Each line is a separate doc in nlp.pipe, so # sent_id would restart at 1 for every line. With renumber_sent_ids, the sentences are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on over the whole text instead. This only matters when the formatter has include_headers=True. With sent_ids, the sentences get your own IDs instead, in order of the output.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default text str

The text to parse.

required n_process int

Number of processes for nlp.pipe. -1 uses all cores. Values other than 1 may not work with UDPipe.

1 renumber_sent_ids bool

Whether to number # sent_id consecutively over the whole text.

True ignore_pipe_errors bool

Whether to skip the checks that raise an OSError when n_process is likely to fail on this system.

False split_on_newline bool

Whether to split the text on newlines and pass every line to nlp.pipe separately. This is faster for long texts.

True sent_ids Iterable[str | int] | None

One ID per output sentence for the # sent_id lines. An ID cannot be empty or contain whitespace. It replaces the generated numbers and renumber_sent_ids has no effect. Requires include_headers=True in the formatter. With disable_sbd=True in init_parser, every input line is one sentence, so you can give one ID per line.

None

Returns:

Type Description str

The CoNLL-U string, with one empty line between sentences. It

str

starts with a # global.columns line when the formatter has

str

columns.

Raises:

Type Description OSError

If n_process is not 1, ignore_pipe_errors is false, and the backend is UDPipe on Windows.

ValueError

If sent_ids is given without include_headers, if an ID is empty or contains whitespace, or if the number of IDs differs from the number of sentences.

Examples:

from spacy_conll import init_parser
nlp = init_parser(
    "en_core_web_sm",
    "spacy",
    disable_sbd=True,
    formatter_config={"include_headers": True},
)
conll = ConllParser(nlp).parse_text_as_conll(
    "I like cookies.\nMe too.",
    sent_ids=["doc1-008", "doc1-009"],
)
[line for line in conll.splitlines() if line.startswith("#")]
# ['# sent_id = doc1-008', '# text = I like cookies.', '# sent_id = doc1-009', '# text = Me too.']

docs.title: parse_conll_text_as_spacy
docs.text:
parse_conll_text_as_spacy(
    text: str,
    *,
    ner_tag_pattern: str = NER_TAG_PATTERN,
    ner_map: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    strict: bool = True,
) -> Doc

Read CoNLL-U text into a spaCy doc.

Sentences are separated by an empty line, and every sentence block becomes one spaCy sentence. Fields that spaCy does not store are kept in extensions: DEPS in Token._.conll_deps_graphs_field, MISC in Token._.conll_misc_field and the comment lines in Span._.conll_metadata of the sentence. A _ in LEMMA, UPOS, XPOS or FEATS leaves that attribute empty in spaCy, and the formatter writes _ again. Multi-word tokens and empty nodes are not supported. Adapted from spaCy's conllu2json converter.

With strict=False, HEAD and DEPREL may be _ (both on the same line), for example in a file that is tagged but not parsed. Such a token has no head in spaCy (token.has_head() is false and token.dep_ is ""), and the formatter writes _ for both fields. The HEAD values of a sentence then do not have to form one tree.

CoNLL-U Plus is supported: when the first line is a # global.columns comment, the lines have these columns in this order. A standard column that is missing gets the value _, and an ID column that is missing gets the token position. Custom columns such as PARSEME:MWE are kept in the dict Token._.conll_custom_columns. The # global.columns line is not part of Span._.conll_metadata. The columns are stored in Doc._.conll_columns, which the formatter uses to write the doc again unless it has its own columns.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default text str

CoNLL-U text.

required ner_tag_pattern str

Regex for the entity tag in the MISC field.

NER_TAG_PATTERN ner_map dict[str, str] | None

Maps old entity labels to new ones. A label that maps to "" becomes O.

None strict bool

Whether every token needs a HEAD and a DEPREL, and the HEAD values of every sentence must form one tree.

True

Returns:

Type Description Doc

A doc with all sentences of the text and the CoNLL extensions.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a line does not have 10 fields (or as many as the # global.columns line lists), a field is empty, a field other than FORM, LEMMA, MISC or a custom column contains a space, ID or HEAD is not a valid number, only one of HEAD and DEPREL is _, or # global.columns has an invalid column name. With strict=True also if HEAD or DEPREL is _, or if the HEAD values of a sentence do not form one tree. The message starts with the line number.

NotImplementedError

If the text has multi-word tokens or empty nodes.

Examples:

import spacy
nlp = spacy.blank("en")
_ = nlp.add_pipe(
    "conll_formatter", config={"include_headers": True}
)
conll = "\n".join(
    [
        "# sent_id = a1",
        "1\tHi\thi\tINTJ\tUH\t_\t0\troot\t0:root\t_",
        "2\tthere\tthere\tADV\tRB\t_\t1\tadvmod\t1:advmod\tSpaceAfter=No",
    ]
)
doc = ConllParser(nlp).parse_conll_text_as_spacy(conll)
[(t.text, t.dep_, t.head.text) for t in doc]
# [('Hi', 'ROOT', 'Hi'), ('there', 'advmod', 'Hi')]
print(doc._.conll_str.replace("\t", " "))
# # sent_id = a1
# 1 Hi hi INTJ UH _ 0 root 0:root _
# 2 there there ADV RB _ 1 advmod 1:advmod SpaceAfter=No

A sentence without dependency annotation needs strict=False:

conll = "1\tHi\thi\tINTJ\tUH\t_\t_\t_\t_\t_"
doc = ConllParser(nlp).parse_conll_text_as_spacy(
    conll, strict=False
)
[(t.text, t.dep_, t.has_head()) for t in doc]
# [('Hi', '', False)]
print(doc._.conll_str.replace("\t", " "))
# # sent_id = 1
# # text = Hi
# 1 Hi hi INTJ UH _ _ _ _ _

View source on GitHub: src/spacy_conll/parser.py lines 268–554

docs.title: Migrating from v4 to v5
docs.text: v5 changes the signatures of init_parser, ConllParser methods and the command line options, and removes the stanza backend. The CoNLL-U output of a given pipeline stays the same.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or newer (v4: 3.8 or newer).
  • spaCy 3.8 or newer.
  • The package is built with hatchling and managed with uv. The version comes from git tags.

docs.title: The stanza backend is removed
docs.text:
spacy-stanza pins stanza<1.7, and those versions cannot load models under current versions of torch. parser="stanza" and the spacy-conll[stanza] extra are gone. Use spacy or udpipe instead:

# v4
nlp = init_parser("en", "stanza")

# v5
nlp = init_parser("en", "udpipe")

The extras are now udpipe, parsers (the same as udpipe), pd and all.

docs.title: init_parser
docs.text:
The **kwargs that went to the formatter are replaced by the explicit argument formatter_config. parser is a Literal["spacy", "udpipe"]. parser_opts is not modified any more.

# v4
nlp = init_parser("en_core_web_sm", "spacy", include_headers=True)

# v5
nlp = init_parser(
    "en_core_web_sm", "spacy", formatter_config={"include_headers": True}
)

The old keyword arguments ext_names, field_names, conversion_maps and disable_pandas move into formatter_config in the same way.

docs.title: ConllParser
docs.text:
parse_text_as_conll and parse_file_as_conll take keyword-only options. no_force_counting and no_split_on_newline are replaced by positive options.

v4 v5 no_force_counting=True renumber_sent_ids=False no_split_on_newline=True split_on_newline=False input_encoding defaults to the system encoding input_encoding defaults to "utf-8" 
# v4
parser.parse_text_as_conll(
    text, n_process=4, no_force_counting=True, no_split_on_newline=True
)
parser.parse_file_as_conll("in.txt", "utf-8", no_force_counting=True)

# v5
parser.parse_text_as_conll(
    text, n_process=4, renumber_sent_ids=False, split_on_newline=False
)
parser.parse_file_as_conll("in.txt", renumber_sent_ids=False)

The signatures are now:

parse_text_as_conll(text, *, n_process=1, renumber_sent_ids=True, ignore_pipe_errors=False, split_on_newline=True)
parse_file_as_conll(input_file, *, input_encoding="utf-8", n_process=1, renumber_sent_ids=True, ignore_pipe_errors=False, split_on_newline=True)

parse_conll_text_as_spacy and parse_conll_file_as_spacy also take keyword-only options, and input_encoding of the file method defaults to "utf-8". The regular expression for entity tags is available as the constant spacy_conll.parser.NER_TAG_PATTERN.

# v4
doc = parser.parse_conll_file_as_spacy("in.conllu", "utf-8")

# v5
doc = parser.parse_conll_file_as_spacy("in.conllu", input_encoding="utf-8")

docs.title: Token._.conll
docs.text: Token._.conll is a plain dict instead of an OrderedDict. Dicts keep the insertion order, so the order of the fields is the same.

docs.title: DEPREL of the root token
docs.text:
The root token has the DEPREL root for every backend, as the CoNLL-U format requires. spaCy models gave ROOT before.

# v4
"0\tROOT"

# v5
"0\troot"

To keep the old label, map it with conversion_maps={"DEPREL": {"root": "ROOT"}}.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
All multi-word options use hyphens instead of underscores, the single-letter flags -a, -b, -c, -s, -t, -d, -e and -j are removed, and the encoding defaults are utf-8. One of -f/--input-file and --input-str is required.

v4 v5 -f, --input_file -f, --input-file -b, --input_str --input-str -a, --input_encoding --input-encoding -o, --output_file -o, --output-file -c, --output_encoding --output-encoding -s, --disable_sbd --disable-sbd -t, --is_tokenized --is-tokenized -d, --include_headers --include-headers -e, --no_force_counting --no-renumber-sent-ids -j, --n_process --n-process --ignore_pipe_errors --ignore-pipe-errors --no_split_on_newline --no-split-on-newline -v, --verbose -v, --verbose 
# v4
parse-as-conll en_core_web_sm spacy -b "I like cookies." -d -j 2

# v5
parse-as-conll en_core_web_sm spacy --input-str "I like cookies." --include-headers --n-process 2

docs.title: Bug fixes that change behavior
docs.text:
• The command line script crashed on every run in 4.0.x. It works again.
  • Adding conll_formatter to a pipeline failed config validation with recent spaCy versions because field_names was None.
  • Pretokenized input with an empty string raised an IndexError. It gives an empty Doc.
  • Empty docs with pandas installed raised an error. They give an empty DataFrame.
  • CoNLL-U text that ends with a blank line raised an error.
  • n_process=-1 skipped the multiprocessing checks.
  • n_process other than 1 works with pandas enabled, and docs can be saved with DocBin. conll_pd is computed from conll when you access it instead of being stored in the doc.
  • Output no longer starts with a newline when the first line of the input is empty.
  • Newlines, tabs and repeated spaces no longer appear as token lines, so the output is valid CoNLL-U (#35). IDs and heads skip the whitespace tokens, the whitespace goes to MISC as SpacesAfter or SpacesBefore, and the whitespace tokens have None as their extensions. See Newlines, tabs and other whitespace.
  • The formatter keeps the MISC entries of a token that was read from CoNLL-U, such as Translit=x, instead of replacing them with _ or SpaceAfter=No.

docs.title: The pipeline component
docs.text:
conll_formatter is a spaCy factory. spaCy finds it through an entry point, so import spacy_conll is not needed before nlp.add_pipe("conll_formatter"). Add it after all components that set tags, lemmas, morphology and dependencies:

import spacy

nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
nlp.add_pipe("conll_formatter", last=True)
doc = nlp("I like cookies.")

init_parser loads a model and adds the formatter in one call. Options for the formatter go in formatter_config:

from spacy_conll import init_parser

nlp = init_parser(
    "en_core_web_sm", "spacy", formatter_config={"include_headers": True}
)

The options of init_parser are:

  • model_or_lang: the spaCy model name or, for UDPipe, a language code such as "en". Models are downloaded automatically for UDPipe only.
  • parser: "spacy" or "udpipe".
  • is_tokenized: the input is a string of tokens that are separated by whitespace. Sentences are then split on newlines only (spaCy) and UDPipe does not support this.
  • disable_sbd: disable sentence boundary detection, so that every input text is one sentence. Only for spaCy.
  • exclude_spacy_components: names of spaCy components to leave out of the pipeline.
  • parser_opts: extra keyword arguments for the loader of the backend (spacy.load). The dict is not modified.
  • formatter_config: the config of conll_formatter, see below.

docs.title: Formatter options
docs.text:
• include_headers: start every sentence with # sent_id = ... and # text = ... comment lines. Default False.
  • ext_names: new names for the extensions conll, conll_str and conll_pd.
  • field_names: new names for the CoNLL-U fields ID, FORM, LEMMA, UPOS, XPOS, FEATS, HEAD, DEPREL, DEPS and MISC. These are the dict keys of ._.conll and the column names of ._.conll_pd.
  • conversion_maps: a dict of the form {field_name: {old_value: new_value}} that replaces output values. The field name is the name after field_names was applied.
  • disable_pandas: do not set conll_pd, even if pandas is installed.
  • columns: a list of CoNLL-U Plus column names that selects and orders the output columns. Default None (plain CoNLL-U). See CoNLL-U Plus.

Unknown keys in ext_names and field_names raise a KeyError.

This example renames conll_pd to pandas and replaces the dependency label nsubj with subj:

from spacy_conll import init_parser

nlp = init_parser(
    "en_core_web_sm",
    "spacy",
    formatter_config={
        "ext_names": {"conll_pd": "pandas"},
        "conversion_maps": {"DEPREL": {"nsubj": "subj"}},
    },
)
doc = nlp("I like cookies.")
print(doc._.pandas)

   ID     FORM  LEMMA   UPOS  ...  HEAD DEPREL DEPS           MISC
0   1        I      I   PRON  ...     2   subj    _              _
1   2     like   like   VERB  ...     0   root    _              _
2   3  cookies  cooky   NOUN  ...     2   dobj    _  SpaceAfter=No
3   4        .      .  PUNCT  ...     2  punct    _  SpaceAfter=No

The same config works with nlp.add_pipe("conll_formatter", config={...}, last=True). Renaming fields changes the keys of the output:

from spacy_conll import init_parser

nlp = init_parser(
    "en_core_web_sm",
    "spacy",
    formatter_config={"field_names": {"UPOS": "upostag", "XPOS": "xpostag"}},
)
doc = nlp("I like cookies.")
print(doc._.conll_pd.columns.tolist())

['ID', 'FORM', 'LEMMA', 'upostag', 'xpostag', 'FEATS', 'HEAD', 'DEPREL', 'DEPS', 'MISC']

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text:
The formatter sets three extensions on every Token, on every sentence Span and on the Doc. Other spans do not get them.

  • ._.conll: the raw data.
    • Token: a dict with the CoNLL-U fields as keys.
    • Sentence Span: a list of the dicts of its tokens.
    • Doc: a list of the lists of its sentences.
  • ._.conll_str: the CoNLL-U text.
    • Token: one tab-separated line that ends with a newline.
    • Sentence Span: one line per token. With include_headers=True the # sent_id and # text lines come first.
    • Doc: the strings of all sentences, separated by an empty line.
  • ._.conll_pd: a pandas object, only available if pandas is installed and disable_pandas is false.
    • Token: a Series.
    • Sentence Span: a DataFrame with the field names as columns.
    • Doc: the DataFrame of all sentences with a new index. A Doc without tokens gives an empty DataFrame with the field columns.
import spacy

nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
nlp.add_pipe("conll_formatter", last=True)
doc = nlp("I like cookies.")
print(doc[0]._.conll)
print(repr(doc[0]._.conll_str))

{'ID': 1, 'FORM': 'I', 'LEMMA': 'I', 'UPOS': 'PRON', 'XPOS': 'PRP', 'FEATS': 'Case=Nom|Number=Sing|Person=1|PronType=Prs', 'HEAD': 2, 'DEPREL': 'nsubj', 'DEPS': '_', 'MISC': '_'}
'1\tI\tI\tPRON\tPRP\tCase=Nom|Number=Sing|Person=1|PronType=Prs\t2\tnsubj\t_\t_\n'

Empty values are written as _. HEAD is the position of the head within its sentence, 0 for the root, and _ for a token without a head (for example in a pipeline without a parser). MISC is SpaceAfter=No for tokens that are not followed by whitespace. Other whitespace is described below.

docs.title: Newlines, tabs and other whitespace
docs.text:
spaCy keeps newlines, tabs and repeated spaces as separate tokens with the tag _SP. The formatter leaves these whitespace tokens out of the output, because a CoNLL-U field cannot contain a tab or a newline. It follows the UD convention and records the whitespace in MISC of the token before it:

  • a single space: no entry (_)
  • no whitespace: SpaceAfter=No
  • any other whitespace: SpacesAfter with the escapes \s (space), \t (tab), \n (newline) and \r (carriage return)
  • whitespace at the start of the doc: SpacesBefore on the first token

The IDs and heads are renumbered without the whitespace tokens. A token whose head is a whitespace token gets the nearest ancestor that is not whitespace as its head, or becomes a root if there is none. The # text line has its whitespace collapsed to single spaces. A sentence that only contains whitespace has no output and does not count for # sent_id.

import spacy

nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
nlp.add_pipe("conll_formatter", last=True, config={"include_headers": True})
doc = nlp("Results are clear.\n2.\t")
print(doc._.conll_str)

# sent_id = 1
# text = Results are clear.
1   Results result  NOUN    NNS Number=Plur 2   nsubj   _   _
2   are be  AUX VBP Mood=Ind|Tense=Pres|VerbForm=Fin    0   root    _   _
3   clear   clear   ADJ JJ  Degree=Pos  2   acomp   _   SpaceAfter=No
4   .   .   PUNCT   .   PunctType=Peri  2   punct   _   SpacesAfter=\n

# sent_id = 2
# text = 2.
1   2   2   X   LS  NumType=Ord 0   root    _   SpaceAfter=No
2   .   .   PUNCT   .   PunctType=Peri  1   punct   _   SpacesAfter=\t

The whitespace tokens themselves have None as ._.conll, ._.conll_str and ._.conll_pd. The sentence and doc extensions only contain the other tokens, so doc[4]._.conll is None here (the token "\n"), and len(doc._.conll_pd) is 6 for the 8 tokens of the doc.

docs.title: Parsing text and files
docs.text:
ConllParser wraps a pipeline that contains conll_formatter, for example the output of init_parser. It raises a ValueError if the component is missing.

from spacy_conll import ConllParser, init_parser

nlp = init_parser(
    "en_core_web_sm", "spacy", formatter_config={"include_headers": True}
)
parser = ConllParser(nlp)
conll = parser.parse_text_as_conll("I like cookies. What about you?")
print(conll)

# sent_id = 1
# text = I like cookies.
1   I   I   PRON    PRP Case=Nom|Number=Sing|Person=1|PronType=Prs  2   nsubj   _   _
2   like    like    VERB    VBP Tense=Pres|VerbForm=Fin 0   root    _   _
3   cookies cooky   NOUN    NNS Number=Plur 2   dobj    _   SpaceAfter=No
4   .   .   PUNCT   .   PunctType=Peri  2   punct   _   _

# sent_id = 2
# text = What about you?
1   What    what    PRON    WP  _   2   dep _   _
2   about   about   ADP IN  _   0   root    _   _
3   you you PRON    PRP Case=Acc|Person=2|PronType=Prs  2   pobj    _   SpaceAfter=No
4   ?   ?   PUNCT   .   PunctType=Peri  2   punct   _   SpaceAfter=No

parse_file_as_conll(input_file) does the same for a text file (input_encoding defaults to "utf-8"). Both methods take these keyword-only options:

  • n_process: number of processes for nlp.pipe. -1 uses all cores. Default 1.
  • renumber_sent_ids: number # sent_id over the whole input. Every line of the input is a separate Doc and spaCy would restart the numbering at 1 for each. Default True. This only matters with include_headers=True.
  • ignore_pipe_errors: skip the checks that raise an OSError when n_process is not 1 and the setup is likely to fail. Default False.
  • split_on_newline: process every line of the input as its own Doc, which is faster for long input. Without it, the whole input is one text. Default True.
  • sent_ids: your own IDs for the # sent_id lines, one per output sentence. Default None. See below.

docs.title: Your own sentence IDs
docs.text:
If your sentences already have IDs, pass them as sent_ids. They replace the generated numbers, so renumber_sent_ids has no effect. This requires include_headers=True. An ID cannot be empty or contain whitespace. The number of IDs must equal the number of sentences in the output, otherwise you get a ValueError. With disable_sbd=True every line of the input is one sentence (empty lines are skipped), so you give one ID per non-empty line:

from spacy_conll import ConllParser, init_parser

nlp = init_parser(
    "en_core_web_sm",
    "spacy",
    disable_sbd=True,
    formatter_config={"include_headers": True},
)
parser = ConllParser(nlp)
conll = parser.parse_text_as_conll(
    "I like cookies.\nWhat about you?", sent_ids=["chat-008", "chat-009"]
)
print(conll)

# sent_id = chat-008
# text = I like cookies.
1   I   I   PRON    PRP Case=Nom|Number=Sing|Person=1|PronType=Prs  2   nsubj   _   _
...

# sent_id = chat-009
# text = What about you?
...

parse_file_as_conll takes the same option. When you read the output back with parse_conll_text_as_spacy, the IDs stay in Span._.conll_metadata of every sentence.

docs.title: Pretokenized input
docs.text:
With is_tokenized=True spaCy splits the text on whitespace only and every line is one sentence:

from spacy_conll import init_parser

nlp = init_parser("en_core_web_sm", "spacy", is_tokenized=True)
doc = nlp("This is , a pretokenized sentence .")
print(doc._.conll_str)

An empty string gives an empty Doc and no output.

docs.title: Reading CoNLL-U into spaCy
docs.text:
parse_conll_text_as_spacy(text) and parse_conll_file_as_spacy(input_file) build a Doc from CoNLL-U. Sentences are separated by an empty line and # comment lines are allowed. The formatter has already run on the returned Doc, so all extensions are available.

from spacy_conll import ConllParser, init_parser

nlp = init_parser(
    "en_core_web_sm", "spacy", formatter_config={"include_headers": True}
)
parser = ConllParser(nlp)

conll = """# sent_id = a1
# text = From the AP comes this story
1\tFrom\tfrom\tADP\tIN\t_\t3\tcase\t3:case\t_
2\tthe\tthe\tDET\tDT\tDefinite=Def|PronType=Art\t3\tdet\t3:det\t_
3\tAP\tAP\tPROPN\tNNP\tNumber=Sing\t4\tobl\t4:obl:from\t_
4\tcomes\tcome\tVERB\tVBZ\tMood=Ind|Number=Sing|Person=3|Tense=Pres|VerbForm=Fin\t0\troot\t0:root\t_
5\tthis\tthis\tDET\tDT\tNumber=Sing|PronType=Dem\t6\tdet\t6:det\t_
6\tstory\tstory\tNOUN\tNN\tNumber=Sing\t4\tnsubj\t4:nsubj\tSpaceAfter=No
"""
doc = parser.parse_conll_text_as_spacy(conll)
for token in doc:
    print(token.text, token.dep_, token.pos_, token.head.text)

From case ADP AP
the det DET AP
AP obl PROPN comes
comes ROOT VERB comes
this det DET story
story nsubj NOUN comes

Both methods have two more keyword-only options for named entities that are stored in the MISC field. ner_tag_pattern is the regular expression that matches the BILUO tag (the default is the constant spacy_conll.parser.NER_TAG_PATTERN) and ner_map renames labels. A label that maps to "" becomes O.

Multi-word tokens and empty nodes (IDs such as 1-2 or 2.1) raise a NotImplementedError. A ValueError names the line of the problem. It is raised for a line without 10 tab-separated fields, an empty field, a space in a field other than FORM, LEMMA and MISC, an ID or HEAD that is not a valid number, a HEAD or DEPREL that is _, and a sentence whose HEAD values do not form one tree. A trailing blank line and Windows line endings are allowed.

A _ in LEMMA, UPOS, XPOS or FEATS is a missing value: the spaCy attribute stays empty (token.pos_ == ""), and the formatter writes _ again.

docs.title: Sentences without dependencies
docs.text:
Use strict=False for CoNLL-U that is tagged but not (completely) parsed. HEAD and DEPREL may then be _, as long as both are _ on the same line. Such a token has no head in spaCy (token.has_head() is false and token.dep_ is ""), and the formatter writes _ for both fields. Every sentence block still becomes one spaCy sentence, and a round trip gives the same CoNLL-U.

conll = """1\tana\tana\tADP\tPRP\t_\t_\t_\t_\t_
2\tŠumaya\tŠumaya\tPROPN\tPN\t_\t_\t_\t_\t_
3\tummā\tummu\tNOUN\tN\t_\t_\t_\t_\t_
"""
doc = parser.parse_conll_text_as_spacy(conll, strict=False)
print(
    [(token.text, token.pos_, token.dep_, token.has_head()) for token in doc]
)

[('ana', 'ADP', '', False), ('Šumaya', 'PROPN', '', False), ('ummā', 'NOUN', '', False)]

A pipeline can then add the missing annotation to the returned Doc. Pass the Doc to nlp and enable only the components that you need, so that the tags from the file are kept. The parser keeps the sentence boundaries of the file. This example runs the parser of en_core_web_sm (which needs tok2vec) on tagged text:

import spacy
from spacy_conll import ConllParser

nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
nlp.add_pipe("conll_formatter", last=True)
parser = ConllParser(nlp)

conll = """1\tI\tI\tPRON\tPRP\t_\t_\t_\t_\t_
2\tlike\tlike\tVERB\tVBP\t_\t_\t_\t_\t_
3\tcookies\tcookie\tNOUN\tNNS\t_\t_\t_\t_\tSpaceAfter=No
4\t.\t.\tPUNCT\t.\t_\t_\t_\t_\t_
"""
doc = parser.parse_conll_text_as_spacy(conll, strict=False)
with nlp.select_pipes(enable=["tok2vec", "parser", "conll_formatter"]):
    doc = nlp(doc)
print(doc._.conll_str)

1   I   I   PRON    PRP _   2   nsubj   _   _
2   like    like    VERB    VBP _   0   root    _   _
3   cookies cookie  NOUN    NNS _   2   dobj    _   SpaceAfter=No
4   .   .   PUNCT   .   _   2   punct   _   _

docs.title: Fields that spaCy does not store
docs.text:
DEPS, MISC and the comment lines have no spaCy equivalent. They are kept in custom extensions, which are registered by the formatter and by ConllParser:

  • Token._.conll_deps_graphs_field: the DEPS value of the token. Default "_".
  • Token._.conll_misc_field: the MISC value of the token. Default "_".
  • Token._.conll_custom_columns: a dict with the values of custom CoNLL-U Plus columns, see CoNLL-U Plus. Default None.
  • Span._.conll_metadata: the comment lines of a sentence, with a trailing newline. Default None.
sent = next(doc.sents)
print(repr(sent._.conll_metadata))
print(doc[2]._.conll_deps_graphs_field, doc[5]._.conll_misc_field)

'# sent_id = a1\n# text = From the AP comes this story\n'
4:obl:from SpaceAfter=No

A round trip from CoNLL-U to spaCy and back keeps these values. When the formatter writes MISC, it only sets or removes the entries SpaceAfter, SpacesAfter and SpacesBefore and keeps all other entries in their order. An existing SpacesAfter stays when spaCy has a space after the token, because spaCy cannot store other whitespace between tokens of a doc that is read from CoNLL-U. With include_headers=True, the formatter writes an existing conll_metadata as the header of a sentence instead of generating # sent_id and # text.

docs.title: CoNLL-U Plus
docs.text: CoNLL-U Plus files have a # global.columns line that lists the columns of the file. The columns can be any subset of the ten CoNLL-U fields in any order, plus custom columns.

docs.title: Writing
docs.text:
Set columns in the formatter config. The names are the canonical CoNLL-U names (ID, FORM, LEMMA, UPOS, XPOS, FEATS, HEAD, DEPREL, DEPS, MISC) or custom names with a namespace, such as PARSEME:MWE. Custom names consist of uppercase letters and colons. A list that is empty, has duplicates or has another kind of name raises a ValueError.

from spacy_conll import ConllParser, init_parser

nlp = init_parser(
    "en_core_web_sm",
    "spacy",
    formatter_config={"columns": ["ID", "FORM", "UPOS", "HEAD", "DEPREL"]},
)
doc = nlp("I like cookies.")
print(doc._.conll_str)
print(doc[1]._.conll)
print(doc._.conll_pd.columns.tolist())

# global.columns = ID FORM UPOS HEAD DEPREL
1   I   PRON    2   nsubj
2   like    VERB    0   root
3   cookies NOUN    2   dobj
4   .   PUNCT   2   punct

{'ID': 2, 'FORM': 'like', 'UPOS': 'VERB', 'HEAD': 0, 'DEPREL': 'root'}
['ID', 'FORM', 'UPOS', 'HEAD', 'DEPREL']

The conll, conll_str and conll_pd extensions of tokens, sentences and docs only have the selected columns. The conll_str of a Doc and the output of ConllParser.parse_text_as_conll start with the # global.columns line. It is written whenever columns is set, also if the list has all ten columns.

A custom column takes its value from the dict Token._.conll_custom_columns and is _ for tokens without that key:

doc[1]._.conll_custom_columns = {"PARSEME:MWE": "1:VID"}

field_names and columns are independent. field_names renames the dict keys and the pandas columns only. columns and the # global.columns line always use the canonical names. With field_names={"UPOS": "upostag"} and columns=["FORM", "UPOS"], the keys of ._.conll are FORM and upostag and the header is # global.columns = FORM UPOS.

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
parse_conll_text_as_spacy and parse_conll_file_as_spacy read a # global.columns first line. Every line must have as many tab-separated fields as there are columns, otherwise a ValueError is raised.

  • A standard column that is missing is read as _. A missing ID is the position of the token in its sentence.
  • Custom columns are stored in Token._.conll_custom_columns.
  • The # global.columns line is not part of Span._.conll_metadata.
  • Without HEAD and DEPREL columns, the tokens have no dependency annotation. This needs strict=False, as for _ in these fields.
from spacy_conll import ConllParser, init_parser

nlp = init_parser(
    "en_core_web_sm",
    "spacy",
    formatter_config={"columns": ["FORM", "HEAD", "DEPREL", "PARSEME:MWE"]},
)
parser = ConllParser(nlp)
text = """# global.columns = FORM HEAD DEPREL PARSEME:MWE
I\t2\tnsubj\t*
take\t0\troot\t1:VID
a\t4\tdet\t1
look\t2\tobj\t1
"""
doc = parser.parse_conll_text_as_spacy(text)
print([(t.i, t.text, t.dep_, t.head.i) for t in doc])
print(doc[1]._.conll_custom_columns)
print(doc._.conll_str)

[(0, 'I', 'nsubj', 1), (1, 'take', 'ROOT', 1), (2, 'a', 'det', 3), (3, 'look', 'obj', 1)]
{'PARSEME:MWE': '1:VID'}
# global.columns = FORM HEAD DEPREL PARSEME:MWE
I   2   nsubj   *
take    0   root    1:VID
a   4   det 1
look    2   obj 1

The reader stores the columns of the header in Doc._.conll_columns. A formatter without columns writes the doc with these columns, so the example above also works with init_parser("en_core_web_sm", "spacy"). A formatter with columns uses its own columns instead. For a doc that is read from plain CoNLL-U, conll_columns is None and the output is plain CoNLL-U. conll, conll_str, conll_pd and the # global.columns line all follow these columns. Parsing raw text with parse_text_as_conll does not set conll_columns.

docs.title: Pandas and multiprocessing
docs.text:
If pandas is installed, conll_pd is available automatically. It is computed from conll when you access it and is not stored in the doc, so docs with conll_pd can be saved with DocBin and processed with n_process other than 1:

from spacy_conll import ConllParser, init_parser

nlp = init_parser("en_core_web_sm", "spacy")
parser = ConllParser(nlp)
conll = parser.parse_text_as_conll(
    "I like cookies.\nWhat about you?", n_process=2
)

n_process=-1 uses all cores. On Windows, UDPipe pipelines fail a check, because the models cannot be pickled. ignore_pipe_errors=True skips this check.

A doc that is loaded from a DocBin(store_user_data=True) has conll and conll_str, and conll_pd is computed again from conll (see examples/example-adding-conll-to-docbin.py).

Put the code that starts processes under if __name__ == "__main__":, as for any use of multiprocessing on Windows and macOS.

docs.title: UDPipe backend
docs.text:
Install the extra with pip install "spacy-conll[udpipe]". The model for a language is downloaded on first use:

from spacy_conll import ConllParser, init_parser

nlp = init_parser("en", "udpipe", formatter_config={"include_headers": True})
print(ConllParser(nlp))
print(nlp("I like cookies.")._.conll_str)

ConllParser(parser=udpipe)
# sent_id = 1
# text = I like cookies.
1   I   I   PRON    PRP Case=Nom|Number=Sing|Person=1|PronType=Prs  2   nsubj   _   _
2   like    like    VERB    VBP Mood=Ind|Tense=Pres|VerbForm=Fin    0   root    _   _
3   cookies cookie  NOUN    NNS Number=Plur 2   obj _   SpaceAfter=No
4   .   .   PUNCT   .   PunctType=Peri  2   punct   _   SpaceAfter=No

is_tokenized and disable_sbd are not supported for UDPipe. The stanza backend was removed in v5, see the migration guide.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
The installation adds the script parse-as-conll. It takes a model or language and a backend, plus either -f/--input-file or --input-str:

parse-as-conll en_core_web_sm spacy --input-str "I like cookies. What about you?" --include-headers

# sent_id = 1
# text = I like cookies.
1   I   I   PRON    PRP Case=Nom|Number=Sing|Person=1|PronType=Prs  2   nsubj   _   _
2   like    like    VERB    VBP Tense=Pres|VerbForm=Fin 0   root    _   _
3   cookies cooky   NOUN    NNS Number=Plur 2   dobj    _   SpaceAfter=No
4   .   .   PUNCT   .   PunctType=Peri  2   punct   _   _

# sent_id = 2
# text = What about you?
...

Parse a file with four processes and write the result to another file:

parse-as-conll en_core_web_sm spacy -f large-input.txt -o large-output.conll --include-headers --n-process 4

The script runs the formatter with disable_pandas=True, so --n-process works without further setup. Options:

  • -f, --input-file and --input-str: the input. One of them is required.
  • --input-encoding: encoding of the input file. Default utf-8.
  • -o, --output-file: write to a file. Without it, the output goes to stdout.
  • --output-encoding: encoding of the output file. Default utf-8.
  • --disable-sbd: every line is one sentence. Not for UDPipe.
  • --is-tokenized: tokens are separated by whitespace and every line is one sentence. Not for UDPipe.
  • --include-headers: write # sent_id and # text lines.
  • --renumber-sent-ids and --no-renumber-sent-ids: see renumber_sent_ids. On by default.
  • --n-process: number of processes. -1 uses all cores.
  • --ignore-pipe-errors: skip the multiprocessing checks.
  • --split-on-newline and --no-split-on-newline: see split_on_newline. On by default.
  • --columns NAME [NAME ...]: write CoNLL-U Plus with only these columns, in this order, and a # global.columns line. Invalid names end the program with an error message.
  • --sent-ids-file: a UTF-8 text file with one sentence ID per line (blank lines are ignored). The IDs replace the numbers in the # sent_id lines and the file needs one ID per output sentence. This implies --include-headers.
  • -v, --verbose: also print to stdout when --output-file is set.

Select columns and use your own sentence IDs (ids.txt has the lines doc1-008 and doc1-009):

parse-as-conll en_core_web_sm spacy --input-str "First one.
Second one." --disable-sbd --columns ID FORM UPOS --sent-ids-file ids.txt

# global.columns = ID FORM UPOS
# sent_id = doc1-008
# text = First one.
1   First   ADJ
2   one NUM
3   .   PUNCT

# sent_id = doc1-009
# text = Second one.
...

Run parse-as-conll -h for the full help text.
